BMW’s i3 Touring Is an Electric Alternative to the Upcoming 3 Series Wagon – Spy Shots
15 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
BMW has so far used the i3 moniker on three different models, and the best-known was likely the original hatch . You know, the quirky-looking ride that hasn’t been a thing for a few years now.
That one was made between 2013 and 2022 at the Leipzig factory in Germany, and it is estimated that some 250,000 units have seen the light of day in total. Then came the electric sedan based on the G20 BMW 3 Series. The model was known as the G28, and it was assembled exclusively for the Chinese market between 2022 and 2026.
Fast forward to present day, and we have a brand new i3 in BMW’s portfolio. We are talking about the NA0 sports sedan, which is based on the Neue Klasse (NAx) platform. Thus, it shares plenty of components with the iX3. BMW unveiled it earlier this year, and production commenced at the Munich factory in Germany a couple of months ago. But so far, the family comprises a single member, the four-door sedan, and as we already know, the automaker is also working on its family-friendlier sibling.
Yep, that would be the BMW i3 Touring, which has been spied in the open on quite a few occasions. This model has also fallen into the hands of the pixel-altering crowd several times, as sketching it out is not that tricky. After all, you have to imagine a long-roof version of the i3 Sedan, with a tailgate opening up into a more generous cargo area, and you have the i3 Touring. This model will be offered as an electric alternative to the upcoming new-gen BMW 3 Series Touring, which is also in the making as we speak.
Photo: SH Proshots Mind you, you shouldn’t confuse the two, because even though they may look quite similar, both inside and out, the i3 is based on the Neue Klasse platform, as mentioned above, whereas the new 3er builds on an updated version of the CLAR construction. The G50 thus shares its nuts and bolts with its predecessor, as well as the G30 5 Series, the G32 6 Series, the G01 and G02 X3 and X4, respectively, the G29 Z4, Toyota’s GR Supra, the 4 Series, and other vehicles.
But we’re not here to talk about BMW’s modern-day compact lineup as a whole, as this story is all about the BMW i3 Touring. After all, a fresh batch of spy shots just ended up in our inbox again, as our vigilant man with the cam had a close encounter of the third kind with the tester as it was being pushed hard at the Nurburgring. And even though we have a very good idea of what it will look like, it still had its front and rear fascias under wraps.
Mind you, the front end will be virtually identical to that of its four-door sibling , and at the rear, it will feature the same taillights and bumper. In fact, the only differences between the two will be longer roofline of the Touring (Bimmer slang for station wagon), the larger rear three-quarter windows, the redesigned rear three-quarter panels, and a tailgate instead of a trunk lid. We also expect a few chassis tweaks, probably with an emphasis on the rear-axle suspension.
Photo: SH Proshots This prototype seems to sit on 20-inch wheels that spin around the red brake calipers, and appears to sport bumpers that are bit more aggressive. Thus, we could be looking at an M Sport model. The interior will carry over from the BMW i3 Sedan, complete with the Panoramic iDrive, the quirky-looking infotainment system, the four-spoke steering wheel, and so on. The rear headroom, however, and the cargo area behind the passenger compartment have been improved compared to the four-door model.
To no one’s surprise, the powertrain family will also carry over. This includes the 40 xDrive, with its 369 brake horsepower, and an 82.8 kWh battery pack that enables a 441-mile (710 km) on the WLTP cycle. The 50 xDrive offers 463 brake horsepower on tap, and has a 108.7 kWh battery pack that increases the range to 567 miles (912 km). Due to the different aerodynamic and presumably more weight, the i3 Touring should offer a slightly lower range, and will probably be a tiny bit less agile.
Both the BMW i3 Touring and the 3 Series Touring are expected to come out of hiding sometime in 2027, and they will launch in Europe shortly after the big unveiling. We wouldn’t hold our breath for the two premium compact station wagon models to make their way to the United States of America, because these things do not necessarily sell like hotcakes over here. But assuming they would, would you really buy one of these over an equivalent crossover? Feel free to tell us all about it in the comments area below.

2026 Paris Motor Show • XPENG Reveals G9L at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, Dubbed As the Ultimate "Large SUV for the AI Era"
5 Fascinating Cars That Wowed the Crowds 40 Years Ago at the Paris Motor Show
11 photos
Photo: Stellantis N.V.
One of Europe’s most prestigious car expos, the Paris Motor Show has witnessed the debut of many intriguing production models and concepts over the years. Four decades ago, the show marked the global debut of several memorable cars and in this article, we’ll revisit the five that received the warmest reception.
For us older enthusiasts, it’s oftentimes surprising that 1986 was forty years ago. I know, logic, one look at the calendar or at my ID makes things pretty darn clear but in the back of my mind, 1986 was somehow sooner.
When looking at some cars from 1986 , that feeling gets enhanced. While several models introduced around that period look forty, or even older, others seem more modern.
Such is the case with the following five, which debuted at the prestigious Paris Motor Show in October 1986. Whether production models or concepts , these 40-year-old cars aged like fine wine and continue to be fascinating.
Saab 900 Cabrio
Photo: Saab Automobile AB Saab is no longer producing cars, but during the mid-1980s, it was punching well above its weight, gaining worldwide recognition for its well-built, high-end models.
At the 1986 Paris Motor Show, the Swedish manufacturer presented a new model in the shape of the 900 Cabrio .
The brainchild of Saab Cars USA president Robert " Bob " Sinclair, who was one of the most important figures in the company’s rise in popularity, the 900 Cabrio initially debuted in concept form at the 1983 Frankfurt Motor Show.
After three years of development work, the production version was shown to the European public for the first time and it was met with universal praise, mainly due to its effortlessly exquisite styling, but also due to its innovative features.
Photo: Saab Automobile AB While based on the fixed roof 900, which was in production since 1978, the drop-top version came with reinforced windshield rather than the typical roll bar found on many of the era’s convertibles, and that only improved the cleanness of the design.
Featuring a heavy-duty, insulated power top with a heated rear window, the 900 Cabrio was one of the world’s first modern open-top models developed to be used all-year-round, regardless of the weather.
The car was praised from the get-go, and the initial batch of US-bound units sold out in a matter of days.
Though surviving examples show their age, clean, well-kept ones rarely look forty years old. The model remains fascinating four decades later and has now morphed into a highly sought-after modern classic.
Citroen Xanthia Photo: Stellantis N.V. Since the show has taken place in France’s capital, local carmakers have made it a habit to present stunning concepts showcasing their skill and vision for the future year after year.
For the 1986 edition, Citroen prepared the debut of the AX city car , which turned out to be pretty popular, but also presented a fun little concept to draw even more attention to their new city car.
That concept was the Xanthia, a name which some European enthusiasts will now recognize since it was used on the large family car range that sold very well on the Old Continent throughout the 1990s.
Photo: Stellantis N.V. However, the initial Xanthia had little to do with a family car. Based on the underpinnings of the then-new AX and sharing some of its visual features, the concept was developed to, as Citroen put it, “ celebrate the joy of living .”
The car impressed with its two-seat, open-top, short-windshield, barchetta styling , which was far more exciting than the original AX, or any variation of the model that came in the years that followed.
Unfortunately, the small, lightweight concept never made it into production and didn’t inspire a similar sporty variant of the AX. Nevertheless, it was one of the most appreciated concepts unveiled at the 1986 Paris Motor Show and it remains fascinating forty years later.
BMW 7 Series E32 Photo: BMW AG. BMW began developing a new flagship luxury sedan as early as 1979 with the aim of creating a high-class car that could one-up rivals Mercedes and their highly-praised S-Class .
The production version of that sedan, which became the second-generation 7 Series, made its major European debut at the 1986 Paris Motor show where it was met with jaws dropped to the floor.
Codenamed E32, it impressed with its sober yet elegant styling, ultra-comfortable interior and near-flawless driving experience.
Photo: BMW AG. The driving experience could be enhanced even further thanks to the availability of a V12 engine, the first such motor offered in a German production sedan since the pre-war period.
Apart from the 5.0-liter, 295-hp flagship V12 engine , the E32 7 Series also showcased innovations like CAN bus electronics, xenon headlights, or electronically-controlled dampers.
The second-gen 7 Series was truly a high-tech luxury sedan that one-upped the S-Class (W126) in more ways than one. It earned high praise for outhandling its rival and became a BMW legend, one that’s still revered forty years later.
Porsche 928 S4 Photo: Porsche AG. Porsche introduced the 928 in 1977 as an alternative and, possibly, a replacement for the original 911.
A clean sheet design, the model moved from sheer sports car territory well into the realms of traditional European grand tourers .
A completely new design that prioritized the needs and wishes of American buyers, it was Porsche’s first front-engine production car, as well as the brand’s first V8-powered model.
Photo: Porsche AG. At the 1986 Paris Motor Show, Porsche unveiled the first major upgrade of the 928 in the shape of the S4. Though it made its public debut a month earlier in Frankfurt, the model now took center stage at an even more prestigious show in full production-ready guise.
At the time of its introduction, the S4 represented the pinnacle of the 928 range. It received significant styling upgrades and a new 5.0-liter DOHC V8 that could deliver 320 hp in the European model and 316 hp in the US-bound variant.
The 928 S4 got rave reviews for its build quality, styling, comfort and effortless performance, being called the ultimate Autobahn cruiser by German automotive journalists.
Though the 928 thankfully didn’t replace the 911, it kept Porsche afloat through tough financial times and became one of the carmaker’s most iconic production models. The S4 represented a huge leap forward in model history , taking performance to the next level and serving as the base for the lightweight Club Sport and the GTS, two legendary high-performance models introduced in the following years.
Peugeot Proxima Photo: Stellantis N.V. During the1980s, Peugeot habitually stunned the Paris Motor Show crowds with spectacular concepts.
It all started in 1984 with the stunning 205 Turbo 16 -based Quasar, which blended Group B rally DNA with futuristic styling.
Two years later, the French manufacturer returned to the show with another futuristic concept that it christened Proxima, after Proxima Centauri, the closest known star outside our solar system.
Photo: Stellantis N.V. Unquestionably the most spectacular car at the show in terms of styling, the Proxima still looks futuristic and few people who see it for the first time will ever guess that it’s forty years old.
Designed by Gérard Welter, the Sci-Fi concept featured a polycarbonate canopy and came with innovative features such as a solar-powered AC system, and a novel, onboard satellite-connected navigation system.
Like the Quasar, it was based on a modified 205 Turbo 16 chassis, which meant it featured 4WD and was powered by a mid-mounted 2.85-liter twin-turbo V6 tuned to produce 680 hp.
While the futuristic supercar never even came close to production, it remains one of the most fascinating concept cars introduced during the 1980s.

Toyota Motor Europe Posts Record Nine-Month Sales, Celebrates With Corolla 60th Anniversary Editions
10 photos
Photo: Toyota Europe
Toyota Motor Europe (TME) , the local subsidiary of the world's largest automaker, Toyota Motor Corporation, has announced its nine-month sales tally for the Old Continent.
Toyota Motor Europe (TME) announced a new record for its Old Continent sales of 936,042 units for the namesake Toyota and the premium Lexus brands during the first nine months of 2026, up a mere 0.6%. The company continues to post its highest strength across the electrified field, with the latter segment accounting for 87% of total sales or 813,623 deliveries.
During the time, battery electric vehicle sales more than doubled to 104,832 units, jumping 136% year-on-year, driven by “strong customer demand” for the Toyota C-HR+, bZ4X, Urban Cruiser, and bZ4X Touring. Lexus, unfortunately, can’t be happy about the performance: it sold 62,597 units from January through September 2026, which is down four percentage points compared to last year.
On the other hand, the namesake Toyota brand managed to compensate and reached 873,445 deliveries, up almost one percentage point. The electrified sales reached 753,665 units and soared by 15%, while the Toyota Professional series, aka the Hilux and Proace families, were at over 113k units.
“Customers are responding strongly to our electrified line-up, with notable growth across both hybrid and battery electric vehicles. The Aygo X Hybrid, introduced last year, is bringing our hybrid technology to more customers, while the Toyota C-HR+, bZ4X and bZ4X Touring are driving our growing BEV presence in Europe,” explains Till Conrad, Executive Vice President – Sales, Toyota Motor Europe.
The new Toyota RAV4 Hybrid and PHEV is going well with 41,697 sales, but the Aygo X, Yaris, C-HR, and Corolla still sold better across Europe. Speaking of the Corolla series, the nameplate celebrates 60 years in 2026 and has sold almost one million vehicles per year, each year, with current all-time deliveries standing at 57 million units and counting.
Today, the Toyota Corolla models are produced at 14 production centers in 11 countries, and the 12th generation consists of hatchback, sedan, and Touring Sports (station wagon) models, plus the related Corolla Cross compact crossover SUV. Unsurprisingly, Toyota says it kept the same recipe all these years, and only adapted it to the current times.
“Corolla’s sustained success is founded on the principles that Toyota applied in creating the original model back in 1966. The vision then was for a high-quality, versatile car at an affordable price. Today, 12 generations later, it remains true to those qualities, having constantly adapted over the years to maintain its place at the heart of the market,” explains the company.
In Europe, the Toyota Corolla was first produced beginning in 1971 from complete knock-down kits and full-scale manufacturing began in 1994, with almost 9.5 million sales originating from the Old Continent. Today, production is located at Toyota Motor Manufacturing UK for the Corolla hatchback and Touring Sports, while the sedan is manufactured by Toyota Motor Manufacturing Turkey.
Additionally, the company celebrates six decades of achievements with the European-built Hatchback, Touring Sports and Sedan 60th anniversary limited edition models . The 60th Anniversary versions of the Hatchback and Touring Sports, built in the UK, have a new and exclusive Boreal Blue metallic paint, presented in a dual-tone style with a contrasting Night Sky Black roof and pillars.
There are also new 17-inch alloy wheels with a contrast matt and machined finish, while the Corolla Sedan gains its own signature Lunar Sky Blue paint and shares the 17-inch wheels, 60th Anniversary badging, scuff plates and carpet mats with its sibling Hatchback and Touring Sports models.

2026 Paris Motor Show • Ford Rolls Out the Ranger MS-RT Champion Edition: You Can Choose Any Color As Long as It Is Black
One-Off 1971 Plymouth Road Runner RTS Pops Up for Sale After 7 Years
19 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
When it comes to classic Mopars, collectors usually hunt the Hemi-powered cars . These cars are rare regardless of the nameplate and model year. However, some Mopars don't need Hemi powerplants to be ultra-rare. The Rapid Transit System cars, for instance, are one-off creations.
What's a Rapid Transit System vehicle, you ask? Well, back in 1970, Plymouth put together a traveling promotional road-show that was supposed to market its muscle cars to young buyers across the US. It was called the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Caravan and visited auto shows, dealerships, and race tracks through 1970 and 1971.
The cars were based on Plymouth's existing models, but they were heavily modified, especially in terms of body work. The concept vehicles, which were true one-of-ones, were customized by various designers.
The 1970 lineup included a Road Runner, a Duster 340, and a six-barrel Cuda . For 1971, Plymouth repainted the Duster and the Cuda while introducing a 1971 version of the Road Runner. When the RTS program ended after the 1971 auto show season, some cars found their way into private hands, while others disappeared.
Three of the four vehicles were eventually tracked down and purchased by renowned collector Steven Juliano. One by one, he acquired the two Road Runners and the 1970 Duster. The fourth car, the 1970 Cuda, remained hidden in a garage for nearly 50 years. It resurfaced in 2023 and sold for a whopping $2.2 million.
As for the Juliano-owned RTS cars, they were auctioned off in 2019, when his entire estate was sold following his passing. The 1970 Road Runner sold for $341,000, while the 1970 Duster changed hands for $264,000. The 1971 Road Runner went under the hammer for $236,000. It's been seven years since then, and the latter is up for sale again.
The one-off 1971 Road Runner was recently included among the lots that will cross the block at Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction in January. The car is still unrestored and in pristine condition, just like it was when it left Juliano's estate.
Built by Chuck Miller of Styline Custom for Chrysler Corporation in 1970, the Road Runner RTS sports an extended front end that's six inches longer than the standard Road Runner. It also has a hand-formed steel mesh grille, flanked by dual horizontal lenses concealing a quad headlamp layout.
The Mopar was also fitted with Ram Air induction scoops, clear taillight lenses, and a recessed deck lid. Miller deleted the steel bumpers and fitted custom black wheels. The Orange Candy paint is complemented by custom pearl white stripes running the entire length of the body. The 3D Road Runner heads on all four fenders serve as side market lights.
The interior remained unchanged, while the drivetrain is a very basic 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8 mated with a three-speed TorqueFlite automatic transmission. This powerplant came standard on the Road Runner in 1971.
How did this car soldier on in such fabulous condition without a restoration? Well, unlike the other RTS cars, this one remained with its builder for decades. Chuck Miller kept the Road Runner until the early 1990s, likely pampering it and keeping it safe from the elements. He then sold the car directly to Steven Juliano.
How much will it fetch? Mecum doesn't provide an estimate as of this writing, but it's safe to say that it will get a lot of attention at Kissimmee 2027. It should sell for a higher sum than it did back in 2019, and I have a feeling that the final bid could exceed $400,000.

source_document.body:
LiveWire is preparing to bring its biggest electric two-wheeler lineup yet to EICMA (Milan Motorcycle Show) next month, including a pair of previously unseen models that will offer a preview of where the electric motorcycle company is headed in 2027.
The company will exhibit alongside its majority shareholder Harley-Davidson at the massive Milan motorcycle show, running November 5-8, where its booth will span everything from STACYC electric balance bikes to the lightweight S4 Honcho platform and the more performance-oriented DUST family.
Perhaps the biggest surprise will be the first public appearance of the new S4 Honcho Skate. LiveWire hasn’t revealed much about the bike yet, other than confirming it will expand the Honcho family when it arrives in 2027. We won’t have to wait until EICMA for all the details, though, as LiveWire says preliminary specs and additional information will be released on November 2.
The Skate will join the S4 Honcho Street and S4 Honcho Trail , giving LiveWire a growing family of lightweight electric motorcycles built around its modular S4 platform. The production-ready Honcho Street will also make its European debut at EICMA before going on sale there immediately after the show. Its U.S. launch is scheduled for next week.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
LiveWire is also continuing to flesh out its newly acquired DUST lineup. After acquiring the assets of Dust Moto earlier this year, LiveWire will show off a production-intent version of the DUST Hightail, which is targeting a 2027 introduction.
Alongside it will be another new model known as the DUST Spur, also planned for 2027. Like the Honcho Skate, details remain thin for now, with preliminary specifications coming November 2 and final production specs and pricing expected in the first quarter of next year.
The expanding lineup is particularly interesting because it shows just how far LiveWire is moving beyond the premium full-size electric motorcycles that defined the brand’s early years.
Between STACYC, the lightweight Honcho models, and the more dirt-focused DUST machines, LiveWire is increasingly building a ladder of electric two-wheelers aimed at riders across a much wider range of ages, experience levels, and budgets.
We’ll get a much better look at the newest rungs on that ladder in just a couple of weeks.

Cadillac Unveils Escalade-V Checo Perez Edition and It's Limited to Just 11 Units
9 photos
Photo: Cadillac
Cadillac's latest special edition model is an Escalade-V variant celebrating Checo Perez's return to Formula 1. The so-called Escalade-V Checo Perez Edition is limited to just 11 units, and they're all for Mexico.
This is an ultra-exclusive performance SUV, numbers-wise. And GM settling on just 11 examples is not your usual happenstance. In case you didn't know, '11' is the racing number used by Perez throughout most of his Formula 1 career. So, there's your connection.
Cadillac unveiled this special edition model earlier this week at the residence of the United States ambassador in Mexico, as Perez himself attended the event. According to the carmaker, Checo was personally involved with the project, from the design process to the official debut.
"Cadillac and Checo Perez share a passion for innovation, precision, and the constant pursuit of excellence," stated GM Mexico exec, Paco Garza. "This edition celebrates more than 20 years of the V-Series legacy and recognizes the career of Checo - an icon of Mexican motorsport who has inspired millions of people, both on and off the track. The result is a truly exclusive offering for our customers, in which luxury, performance, and Mexican pride converge in a unique SUV."
A quick look at these cars is unlikely to reveal what's special about them. It's only after a closer inspection that you might notice a few differences. For instance, each vehicle will feature two individually numbered plaques, one on the B-pillar and one on the center console. Both identify the production number (1/11 through 11/11) and Perez's signature.
Buyers can choose between black and white exterior configurations, to go with contrasting black and white interiors - much like the livery of the Formula 1 car . Other noteworthy features include the black Escalade and V-Series badges, monochromatic Cadillac emblems front and rear, sports pedals, a visible carbon fiber V-Series engine cover, and special mirror-mounted projectors blasting V-Series graphics onto the ground.
As for the performance, the engine is completely stock and you get the same 682 horsepower and 653 lb-ft of torque as you would in any other Escalade-V .
Photo: Cadillac "Mexico has always been with me in every race," said Cadillac F1 Team driver, Sergio Perez. "That's why knowing that this special edition exists to celebrate that history makes me incredibly excited. I hope that the customers who own one of these 11 units enjoy them just as much as I enjoyed being part of this project - a project I was involved in from the design phase all the way to the unveiling of this special edition."
Two things. First, I'm personally curious why Cadillac went with the Escalade-V instead of something a little more... agile, like say the CT5-V Blackwing or the CT4-V Blackwing. If I had to guess, I'd say it's because they can charge way more for the Escalade-V, but ultimately, who knows?
Second, where's Valtteri Bottas' special-edition Caddy? Well, Cadillac doesn't sell any vehicles in Finland, officially; so that might explain it. However, Bottas is known to reside in Australia, where Cadillac sells the Optiq, Lyriq and the Vistiq, but more importantly, the Lyriq-V. They could make a special edition from one of those... just saying.

Porsche Mission S Hits the Streets of New York for the First Time
18 photos
Photo: Porsche | Instagram
The all-new Porsche Mission S has just hit the streets of New York. The concept car moved from its world premiere stage onto the public roads of Manhattan and Brooklyn. Official photos show it navigating real NYC traffic near the High Line and across the DUMBO trendy neighborhood.
Porsche's new supercar concept rides low, wide, and aggressively aerodynamic, seemingly trying but failing to fly under the radar. With that striking silhouette finished in silver, it is next to impossible for the Mission S to keep a low profile.
Porsche chose New York for the premiere of its Mission S on October 15. The official unveiling of the concept car took place at the Sound River Studios, a waterfront venue located on a historic pier in Long Island City in Queens.
Porsche deliberately chose this exact location for the event for its historical significance: it is the exact same Queens pier where the first global press photos of the iconic mid-engined Porsche 550 Spyder were taken back in 1953.
The Mission S shares a direct spiritual and engineering connection with the 550 Spyder. While their tech is decades apart, Porsche designed the Mission S as a nod to its 1950s ancestor in terms of engineering, design cues, and cockpit layout.
Just like the 1953 Porsche 550 Spyder, the Mission S comes with a mid-engine architecture. By putting the engine in the middle, the automaker altered the typical supercar proportions in favor of a balanced stance, designed entirely for performance.
Furthermore, the all-new supercar features prominent “torpedo” fenders that rise higher than the front hood. It is a classic Porsche design cue that started with the brand’s earliest race cars, including the 550 Spyder and the 356, allowing the driver to see the edges of the front wheels from the cockpit.
In the meantime, the top-mounted cooling fan echoes the iconic design of the 917 , which gave Porsche its first overall win at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1970 and 1971. Meanwhile, the "telephone dial" wheels are a throwback to the 928 luxury grand tourer, which debuted in 1977 as a 1978 model year.
Porsche hasn’t disclosed any details about the engine that powers the Mission S , but the automaker is reportedly secretly developing an all-new flat-eight engine specifically for the production version of this concept car.
The photos taken in New York show the concept car in motion, so it has to have something behind the seats, unless Porsche is trying to trick us by showing us an empty shell photoshopped with the motion effect to make us believe that it really is moving on its own power. One thing is for sure: it will not be an EV.
When will the production version arrive? Porsche is keeping that information under wraps as well. The only thing leaked about this car was the footage that showed up online just hours before the global premiere last week, and that was it. An Icon, Reinvented: The Coachman VIP 575 Travel Trailer Is Better Than Ever for 2027
28 photos
Photo: Coachman Caravans
"The road to freedom" might be twisted or long or even still a mystery when you set out, but it should include a premium travel trailer from Coachman Caravans. Or so says Coachman in their decades-old mantra and logo, with full applicability for the models in their signature range, the VIP.
With a name like that, you should only expect the best of the best. The VIP series of travel trailers from Coachman is comprised of five floorplans for the 2027 model year, all of them single axle and all of them centered on offering a premium experience onboard.
The VIP series is closing on 40 years of existence, but they're aging like fine wine. It's the signature and flagship series from the esteemed British RV specialist, embodying the Coachman spirit and dedication to a product well made. The VIP travel trailers are one step down from the newer Lusso models we checked out recently, but they're still premium – and absolutely gorgeous as well.
The VIP 575 is the largest of the five entries in the VIP series but still a single-axle model. Coachman has chosen it as a highlight for the updates introduced for 2027, from the new graphics and new diamond-cut alloy wheels to the overhauled interiors, with re-engineered cabinetry, new hardware, new upholstery, and lots of modern tech.
Photo: Coachman Caravans Coming in at 7.43 meters (24.3 feet) of length, the VIP 575 is built on an AL-KO galvanized steel chassis and comes standard with AL-KO stabilizer and shock absorbers. Other features mentioned in the introductory video tour below, like the wheel lock and AL-KO ATC, are available but only as paid upgrades.
The VIP 575 is built with aluminum sandwich construction sidewalls and sandwich roof and floor, double-glazed plastic windows, and the now-iconic Coachman oversized windshield that turns the space up front into an atrium-like space. That last one comes very in handy in the VIP 575, where you get a face-to-face seating area slash dining room slash secondary bedroom.
This floorplan offers sleeping for four people maximum and it's one of the most popular in the entire range. Despite its relative family-friendliness , it's actually preferred as a couple's floorplan, since it features a rear bathroom that has the guests sleeping up front passing through the main, fixed bedroom to reach it. In a midnight emergency, this solution is less than ideal, as you must agree.
Photo: Coachman Caravans Still, you have a double bed at the front, should you ever need it. During the day, it transforms into a nice seating area on dual facing couches, with a small pull-out snack/games table coming out of the piece of furniture at the very front.
The slatted extension that joins the couches into a bed is also tucked in there, while the larger dining table is a movable one that stores in a dedicated cabinet by the door.
New for 2027 in this space is the cabinetry, which has been redesigned with rounded edges, new woods, new finishes, black hardware, and soft-close hinges throughout. The soft-touch upholstery and the selection of pillows are also new, as are the acoustic panels on the walls at the front end in the lounge.
Photo: Coachman Caravans From the lounge to the kitchen is but a step, but Coachman does its best to separate the two areas visually, if not physically. An L-shaped kitchen block with new composite counters for more workspace, a flip-up extension, and a sink insert takes up center stage and delivers real home comforts.
This space comes equipped with a four-burner hybrid cooktop (three burners on gas and one hotplate), a large oven, a separate grill, a new extractor, and a flat-bed microwave. The new backsplash matches the composite counter, while cabinetry has been optimized to offer more storage volume. A Thetford fridge with freezer is tucked under the counter across the way.
The bedroom is located in the center of the trailer , so it's essentially a pass-through one. Coachman does its best to turn a con into an advantage, adding a tilting bed with a large storage compartment underneath (also accessible from the outside), overhead lockers, and matching wardrobes with nightstands on either side.
Photo: Coachman Caravans A "luxurious" headboard adds a touch of sophistication, while under-mounted reading lights and USB outlets add convenience. The mattress is on gas-assisted struts and sits on a slatted, ventilated base.
The bathroom runs the full width of the trailer and it's very much a residential one in functionality. It features a walk-in shower with glass doors on the campside, a raised bowl on a vanity with storage, and a cassette toilet with a ladder-style tower heater. Hardware is black, like in the rest of the trailer, with backsplash that matches the one in the kitchen, and excellent lighting.
The VIP 575 comes with dual lockers at the front , one for a pair of gas bottles and the other for storage, a new door with central locking, a new touchscreen control panel, a Thatchcam-approved Scorpion S7 tracker, and Alde wet central heating that runs under the floor and provides instant hot water. This is a year-round caravan that can further be upgraded by adding options from a list: ATC, secure wheel lock, a 120W Truma flexible solar panel, a Truma AC unit, 4G WiFi, or a chassis upgrade.
Photo: Coachman Caravans Speaking of upgrading the weight, standard configuration brings you a towable tipping the scales at 1,511 kg (3,331 lbs) empty, with 1,667 kg (3,675 lbs) of maximum permissible weight.
Prices for the 2027 Coachman VIP 575 start at £38,430 for 2027, which would be roughly €45,800 or $51,500 at the current exchange rate. Since these trailers are only sold locally within the UK, those numbers are for reference only.

Tarran's L1 Series Cargo E-Bikes Are Tech-Laden Beasts That You Can Even Park and Store Vertically
11 photos
Photo: Tarran
Last year, the world would witness the name Tarran for the first time ever when they unveiled their T1 series. It made headlines with a longtail design that called upon “landing gear, ” among others, in order to assist its user in loading it up to the teeth with cargo.
The T1 was so out there and unique that it was even granted the prestigious Red Dot award back in 2025, and as if seeking to continue their cargo-carrying heritage in excellence, Tarran chose to also create an e-bike for 2026, unveiling the L1 lineup, two e-bikes – soon to be three - that go above and beyond to literally replace your car.
Now, where the T1 differed from all others on the market, the L1 comes in with a more traditional cargo e-bike design, calling upon a long tail format and a rear construction that allows users to mix and match accessories to their needs and budgets.
Photo: Tarran As a cargo e-bike, the L1 is designed to handle quite the load, be it on the bike itself or towed along behind. A maximum of 215 kg (474 lbs) is the limit for this one, including rider, bike, and cargo. The bike itself weighs 37.5 kg (83 lbs) on its own, and without a battery. This leaves us with close to 170 kg (375) to work with, which is plenty for a plump rider and still have room left over for kids on the back.
Speaking of which, like most cargo e-bikes out there, an array of accessories are available to choose from in order to tune the L1 to your lifestyle. This includes pet and child carriers, grocery baskets, and even covers to protect all your precious goodies.
Before moving on, I want to point out a bit of a trick that the L1 has up its sleeves. At the rear of the cargo rack, Tarran added a couple of roller wheels that act as supports to help owners store their L1 in garages, but on a vertical plane, or upright, with the front wheel completely off the ground . This ability is also there to help us stick the L1 into an elevator.
Photo: Tarran As for the power to get you and your goodies moving, it’s all due to a mid-mounted motor that drives the rear wheel with either a belt or chain-driven transmission; the L1S is belt-driven, and we’ll talk about why shortly, and the L1M is the chain-driven one.
Both, however, are rocking the same motor system, able to spit out a peak of 750 W and 100 Nm )74 lb-ft) of torque, enough to rival some of Bosch’s most powerful units, and ample spunk to get us moving under load.
Yet, the most important difference between the two models is the transmission. As mentioned, on the L1S, we have a belt setup, and to offer gear range to such a system is impossible with traditional derailleurs and gear cassettes. So, Tarran has called upon a top-shelf Enviolo internal gear hub with Stepless shifting, meaning we can tap into infinite gear range between its lowest and highest .
Photo: Tarran The important takeaway here is that this system is one that can be tuned to make automatic shifts for you. All you have to do is set the cadence and hard and software does the rest. It’s also this component, among what the bike can achieve on its own, that racks up a price tag for the L1S of as much as €5,500 ($6,200), up from €3,800 ($4,264) that the L1M rolls in at, and that’s not including any accessories.
What I do want to point out about the Enviolo system is that it's receiving some mixed reviews out there, with some riders loving it, with others preferring the traditional chain and cassette setup. The latter mention that there are sluggish points in the Eviolo’s use and that limited range, equivalent to 11-42T, is not always sufficient for their needs.
The motor and automatic shifting, along with all the other electronics on this one, will be sucking juice out of a 693 Wh battery that, according to Tarran, is suitable for up to 170 km (106 miles) of riding in Eco mode and unloaded with a 70 kg (154 lbs) rider, a condition you’ll rarely encounter considering this one’s a cargo-loving beast.
Keep in mind that features like Tarran’s vision unit, the system responsible for a rear-view function, the electronic dropper post, and SyncStand, this brand’s electronically activated kickstand, all tap into the battery for juice, so 170 km is something you’ll probably never see; don't forget about navigation services too.
Photo: Tarran The whole thing is also built around 20-inch tires with 2.4 inches of cross-section, and while these rubbers won’t be the best source of softness for riders, there is a suspension fork in place that will reduce some of the hits the road throws at you.
Why 20-inch wheels you may be wondering? It has a whole lot with lowering this e-bikes center of gravity as low as possible. This is meant to keep you stable while loading and unloading cargo, or while taking turns. The last thing you want is to tip over in a turn while your kids are on the rear, and a lower center of gravity helps keep that in check.
While I've never ridden the L1 myself, L1 myself, I've done some research and riders are receiving this one considerably well, despite its premium price tag and head-scratching tech. Weight is a reported downside of the L1 series.
Photo: Tarran Come to think of it, the best way to see if this one’s for you is to find one in a shop near you and take it out for a spin. Oh, and for all you interested riders from the US, Tarran does have a dedicated page where NA residents can get their hands on this one.
Keep in mind that starting Nov 9, as if after EICMA is done, Tarran USA is launching the L1H , the most affordable option for this class, the reason being it has a hub motor. Head on over to their website, sign up for news, and stay patient. Ride safe out there; wear a helmet.

The premium Bavarian automaker BMW has a lot of upcoming new and refreshed models, and some of them are feisty while others are quite practical. No worries, all of them will appear in due time – or a little in advance, sometime.
BMW is currently ready to pay insane money – up to $730k – to its employees to quit, as it wants to get rid of 8k of its workforce by the end of 2027, according to a recent report. They’re reshaping the manpower, but the upcoming new models won’t be affected. At least that’s clear from the latest spied prototypes – our spy photographers can’t get enough camera memory to cover all the upcoming BMWs.
Those include the upcoming BMW i3 Touring but also the high-performance BMW M3 and M5 models, of which one is all-new and coming with both ICE and EV options and the other is a classic LCI – or Life Cycle Impulse – aka a mid-cycle refresh procedure. There are even more on the horizon, even though BMW just unveiled the first-ever iX4 and a bunch of new engine options across the board, among other things.
Of course, the rumor mill is highly invested in the performance BMWs, and a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI has decided to cover the hot subject of the upcoming M5 facelift .
So, later this year or early in 2027 for the 2027 or 2028 model year, the refreshed BMW M5 will arrive complete with revised styling and, once again, the electrified V8 under the hood. The current eighth generation BMW 5 Series G60 was introduced in the spring of 2023, and the G90/99 BMW M5 sedan and M5 Touring quickly appeared during the same year.
As such, it’s not too old, but BMW is hurrying to bring to Neue Klasse snuff all of its most important models, and the 5 Series and M5 will follow in the footsteps of the flagship 7 Series and i7 but feature Neue Klasse styling both inside and outside on this occasion, according to the most recent spied prototypes.
Now, Andrei Avarvarii, the virtual artist behind Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (also known as ' avarvarii ' on social media), has taken a thorough, in-depth CGI look at BMW's upcoming plans and decided to ‘unmask’ the BMW M5. Free from the constraints of the dizzying camouflage, the unofficial, hypothetical BMW M5 design project shows a tamer version of the Neue Klasse styling, as, unlike the latest BMW 3 Series, for example, it will keep the separate kidney grilles.
Otherwise, the rendering is inspired by the latest Neue Klasse models, as seen in the headlight and LED daytime running lights treatment or the front bumper style. The profile won’t change much, and most likely the rear won’t be touched extensively, either. On the other hand, we surely expect the BMW 5 Series and M5 to switch to the controversial BMW Panoramic Vision for the cockpit. Two-Row Mazda CX-90 Purportedly Replaces CX-70 for 2027 in the US
18 photos
Photo: Mazda
Mazda may be replacing the CX-70 in the US with the CX-90 next model year. The catch is that its purported replacement would lose its third row of seats, and the alleged successor would only come in two six-cylinder grades for 2027.
From the standpoint of sales, it sure makes a lot of sense. Through September 2026, year-to-date deliveries totaled 9,686 and 34,999 units, respectively. That's a humongous difference that favors the larger sport utility vehicle in Mazda's lineup for North America, and that's not all. To understand how poorly the CX-70 performed so far in 2026, even the 3 hatchback sold better, moving 11,351 units.
The question is, why did the CX-70 fail so hard? There are many different ways to explain this, but most of all, way too similar pricing and weak differentiation over the CX-90 made the larger sibling the superior buy. As of this writing, Mazda's build and price tool for the US market lists 2026 models from $39,300 for the CX-90 and $42,750 for the less practical CX-70, sans destination charge.
Per the folks at Driving, the company is certain to discontinue the CX-70 stateside even though the US newsroom hasn't been updated with releases for the 2027 models. The cited publication awaits confirmation for the Canadian market regarding a similar change. Looking at the bigger picture, Mazda is most likely to cut its losses across North America rather than the United States market alone.
For model year 2027, the purported two-row version of the CX-90 will stop at only two grades: 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport and 3.3 Turbo S Premium Sport. The former trim presently slots above the entry-level 3.3 Turbo Select and the better-equipped 3.3 Turbo Preferred in the US range.
Photo: Mazda When equipped with three rows, the 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport retails at $47,480 in the United States of America. The S will set you back a cool $54,140 before taxes and optional extras, but you do get a bit more oomph from the inline-six turbo gasser underhood. The numbers are 280 hp with 332 lb-ft (450 Nm) and 340 hp with 369 lb-ft (500 Nm), respectively.
Mazda recommends 87 regular unleaded for the regular-output motor, whereas the high-output specification takes 91 premium dino juice. Third-row versions of the CX-90 soldier on with seven- or eight-seat layouts, and unfortunately, the plug-in hybrid 2.5 naturally aspirated I4 will only be offered with three rows.
In optimal conditions, the plug-in setup develops 323 hp and 369 lb-ft (500 Nm). Electric driving is made possible by a 17.8-kWh battery, which enables a range of 26 miles (42 kilometers). Total range is estimated at 490 miles (789 kilometers), while fuel economy on the four-pot gasoline mill alone is 25 mpg (9.4 l/100 km) in the EPA's combined test cycle.
Beyond these changes, Driving further understands that Mazda plans a small chassis update for the 2027 model year CX-90. More to the point, a new rear suspension crossmember may be coming for improved passenger comfort. Four new paint colors may be on the menu as well: Zircon Sand Metallic, Aero Grey Metallic, Navy Blue Mica, and Melting Copper Metallic.
